question: Pralidoxime (PAM) can effectively reactivate acetylcholinesterase (AChE) in organophosphate poisoning regardless of when it is administered.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. PAM has a strict 24–48 hour window. Once the organophosphate–AChE complex undergoes 'ageing', the bond is permanent and PAM is ineffective. Atropine remains effective throughout (it does not depend on AChE activity), but PAM does not.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Incorrect. PAM must be given within 24–48 hours of OP exposure. After this window, the OP–AChE bond 'ages' (undergoes dealkylation, becoming irreversible) and PAM cannot reactivate the enzyme. Early administration is critical.
